chapter: CBS, return to Ellington and retirement
title: Women's prison programs
summary: The firm worked on helping released women at Alderson, West Virginia, and put on musical programs.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: When you were working with your cousin's consulting firm, what types of consulting did the firm do? In what areas?

She was mostly interested in womens' prisons. We used to go down to Alderson, West Virginia to the prison down there, and they put on programs. And she was trying to set up a system whereby when the girls were released, they would have somewhere to go. In fact, she set up tributaries all over the country now to take the girls, you know, and try to get them jobs and things. And it's been fairly -- fairly successful.
And what -- you worked on the program--
I mostly stayed around the office. I went down to the prison a couple of times, and we gave a program down there once. Not we, because I wasn't playing.
You're talking about -- when you say gave a program, you're talking about entertainment?

Put on a program. Yes, put on a program there. Which the girls seemed to enjoy. The idea was to kind of relieve them of that monotony. Although that is a beautiful place down at Alderson. And they still, you know, get tired of it. So, they would put these programs on to try to relieve the monotony for the girls.
Sort of -- yes, mostly musical, and

mostly the girls themselves were the participants. They had several girls that had nice voices, and quite a bit of talent which they would try to develop, you know, and get the girls to, when they came out, try to, you know, further their talent.
